source_line: Sources: UN Demographic Yearbook 2024, CIA World Factbook

cross_check.name: CIA World Factbook, final edition (Jan 2026, public domain)

items.notes: UN DYB value 17,098,246 km² is Russia within internationally recognised borders (it excludes Crimea and the areas annexed since 2014/2022; Rosstat's own post-2014 figure is about 17.13M km²). Russia straddles Europe and Asia; counted under Europe (UN M49 region: Eastern Europe).

World Bank's 2024 surface-area series shows 15,634,410 km² for Canada, which is not comparable (anomalous since 2015 in the WB/FAO series) and is not used.

insights.text: Next: South Sudan, the world's newest country. Its 2011 split took a quarter of Sudan.
Next: Venezuela, just 5,922 km² ahead of Nigeria in UN data. Other atlases flip them.
Next: Chad and Peru, only 1,216 km² apart. That's barely bigger than Hong Kong.
Greenland (2.17M km²) is self-governing and listed apart from Denmark; alone it'd be 13th.
By land alone, China (9.33M km²) beats the US (9.15M km²), and Canada falls to 4th.
Next: Russia. Often called bigger than Pluto, it isn't: Pluto's surface is ~17.7M km².

scope_note: What counts: total area (land plus inland water such as lakes and rivers) of each sovereign country, as reported in the UN Demographic Yearbook 2024 (Sudan, missing there: World Bank/FAO), cross-checked with the CIA World Factbook. Not counted: Antarctic claims and territories the UN lists separately (Greenland, French overseas regions, Western Sahara; with it Morocco would rank 39th). Disputed areas follow each country's UN figure: India's includes all of Kashmir it claims, Pakistan's excludes the parts it administers, Ukraine is within its recognised borders.

layout.image_prefer: the exact named natural landscape or landform, the classic recognisable view, wide landscape, vivid natural colour, no people as the main subject, no modern buildings, no maps or flags
